title: Scheduling Highest-Priority Work First

guide.problem: Choose the next most important item efficiently.
guide.design: A heap keeps the best candidate at the top. Sorting is better when all results are needed once in order.
guide.invariant: Parent/child priority order holds after insertion and removal.
guide.failure: Assuming every position is globally sorted misreads a heap. Mutating a queued priority without repair breaks the top guarantee.
guide.trace: Insert 4,9,2 into a max-heap; top is 9, then 4 after removing 9.
guide.maintenance: State tie rules when equal-priority tasks must have a stable service order.
guide.scope: This panel connects this listing to its chapter’s problem. Short demonstrations illustrate one part; the chapter’s complete implementation and invariant labs test the broader contract.
